title: Acknowledgements
html:
Acknowledgements

Much of what I know about production systems came from working through problems with other engineers.

I am grateful to the colleagues who took the time to explain an unfamiliar system, question a design, investigate a production failure with me, or share an idea that changed how I approached a problem. Some of the lessons in these chapters began during incidents, but the deeper understanding often came later, when we returned to the evidence and asked why the system had produced the outcome we observed.

I am equally grateful to the engineers who document their work publicly. Postmortems, technical articles, conference talks, and open-source projects have given me access to failures and engineering decisions far beyond those I could encounter in my own work. Accounts that include what failed, what the engineers learned, and what they changed have been especially valuable.

My thanks also go to the mentors, managers, and teammates who trusted me with problems I had not encountered before, gave me room to work through them, and offered guidance when I needed it.

To my family and friends, thank you for your patience, encouragement, and support while I wrote this book. It required many evenings and weekends that would otherwise have been spent with you. I could not have completed it without your support.

And to you, the reader, thank you for giving this book your time. I hope something in these chapters helps you understand a production failure, question an assumption before it becomes an incident, or make a better engineering decision when the evidence is incomplete.

Any errors are mine.
